We have carbon NMR shifts list. Need number of C=O groups. Carbonyl carbons typically appear around 160-220 ppm (for ketones, aldehydes, esters, acids). The given shifts are all low (88.85 down to 14). No high shift, so likely zero carbonyls. Could also be a carbohydrate (C-O). So answer 0.

But ensure no other data needed. Could also use IR to confirm C=O stretch. But carbon NMR already suggests none. To be safe, maybe check IR for carbonyl stretch. Use ir_spectra tool.
